svg.title: Sources of phosphorus reaching Lough Neagh
svg.desc: Provisional split for the Lough Neagh catchment from the July 2024 Lough Neagh Report and Action Plan: agriculture 56%, wastewater treatment works 31%, septic tanks 1%, other sources such as forestry and urban areas 12%. A 2021 model gives 61, 29, 1.3 and 9%. Across all of Northern Ireland a 2020 estimate gives 62% agriculture, 24% wastewater works and 12% septic tanks. Stored phosphorus in soils and the lough bed keeps feeding blooms for years.
svg.text: Where Lough Neagh’s phosphorus comes from
Provisional source split for the Lough Neagh catchment, Lough Neagh Report and Action Plan (July 2024). Other models differ by a few points.
A 2021 model gives 61% agriculture, 29% wastewater, 1.3% septic tanks, 9% other.
Across all of Northern Ireland (2020 estimate) the split is 62% agriculture, 24% wastewater works, 12% septic tanks.
Phosphorus already stored in soils and in the lough bed keeps feeding blooms for years after inputs fall.
